newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish leftists and police clash at protest.
newsitem.headline: Turkish leftists and police clash at protest.

text.p: Rival Turkish left-wing groups fought each other and police on Wednesday at a demonstration to mark the fourth anniversary of a suspected arson attack in which 37 people died, witnesses said.
Several hundred protesters clashed, throwing bottles, sticks and rocks at their rivals and at police, who intervened with batons to break up the fighting.
Two policemen and a number of demonstrators were slightly injured in the fighting at the protest march in central Ankara, which drew a crowd of around 20,000.
There were no reports of protesters being taken into custody.

The demonstration was organised to commemorate the deaths of 37 intellectuals from the liberal Alevi Moslem sect who died when Islamist militants rioted and set fire to a hotel in the central Anatolian town of Sivas in 1993.
